English speaker notes — companion to speaker-notes.zh-CN.txt
Historical v3 presentation; use the latest ten-intent guide for current assignments.

Slide 1 — Research question and prototype scope (35 s)

Our project studies text selection and candidate robot signing for a limited set of expressions. Given English or a phrase button, it selects an explicit ID and previews the corresponding robot motion. We currently study three candidates, all awaiting language comprehensibility validation. This presentation follows two questions: can text select the right ID, and can the robot represent reference movements under its morphological constraints?

Delivery check: do not claim arbitrary-English translation or hospital service.
Sources:
  https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_ros/tree/5994d4faef0a9cadd3287f8de0199a67eeb2a259/robots/g1_description
  README.en.md
  data/catalog.json

────────────────────────────────

Slide 2 — Scenario, alternatives, and scope (60 s)

We imagine brief reception-desk interactions, but that is a future scenario hypothesis. Text displays, human signing, and robot expression address different parts of communication. Repeatable robot movement lets us inspect morphology and paths. The catalog contains HELLO, THANK_YOU, and PLEASE_WAIT. The last ID remains for compatibility; its source supports only a WAIT lexical example, not a complete polite request. ASL is also distinct from Singapore's SgSL; local deployment would need language requirements reassessed.

Delivery check: explain the distance between the present research and imagined application.
Sources:
  docs/实施路线.en.md
  docs/source-review.en.md
  data/catalog.json
  https://sadeaf.org.sg/sgsl-course/

────────────────────────────────

Slide 3 — Shared contracts and error isolation (65 s)

There are two independent acceptance lines. Shared rejection checks precede exact, embedding, or local-model selection. Four statuses exist; non-execute states carry no action. Selection still requires separate preview consent, blocking unreviewed motion by default. The local page runs selection live but plays MP4 prerendered framewise with real MuJoCo, not live browser physics. Separate modules localize selection and geometry errors independently.

Delivery check: where does each interface detect language versus motion failure?
Sources:
  contracts/interfaces.json
  src/sign_robot/pipeline.py
  src/sign_robot/server.py
  src/sign_robot/language.py

────────────────────────────────

Slide 4 — Degrees of freedom and control boundaries (65 s)

The official Unitree model is pinned to a commit with per-file hashes. Fifty-three counts scalar coordinates including passive joints, not independent motors. Twelve mimic relations remain. The scene has zero actuators and directly replays qpos; acceptance concerns kinematic geometry, not controller tracking, torque feasibility, or hardware safety. Independent finger adduction and head/facial expression are absent, limiting language fidelity.

Delivery check: answer control questions with kinematic playback and name untested dynamics.

Slide 5 — Calibration from public videos (75 s)

A1 actually played ASLU THANK_YOU and WAIT and inspected paused frames. THANK_YOU starts near lips with inward palm, moves forward/slightly down, and ends palm-up. Images here are our robot renders; listed seconds belong to source observations, not the same robot timestamps or precise human 3D labels. The robot retains face clearance, different finger spacing, and no smile. Reference video fixes visible discrepancies but cannot establish millimeter human-retargeting error or comprehension.

Delivery check: identify the separate video and robot time axes.

  https://www.lifeprint.com/asl101/pages-signs/t/thankyou.htm

────────────────────────────────

Slide 6 — IK, interpolation, and checks (75 s)

Authored wrist position/orientation/time targets produce named-joint positions[T,53]. Bounded numerical IK considers position, rotation, previous posture, and selected distance penalties. Cubic smoothstep has zero segment-end velocity but no guaranteed acceleration continuity. Twelve intermediate THANK_YOU poses prevent upward fingertip detours from endpoint-only joint interpolation. All frames are checked for limits, velocity, coupling, and available upstream collision geometry. No penetration deeper than 1 mm does not establish complete safety. WAIT retains finger-coupling and full-request gaps.

Delivery check: why does low IK residual not establish correct signing?

Slide 7 — Methods and shared conditions (65 s)

Exact matching accepts complete registered phrases. Local MiniLM uses real 384-dimensional embeddings, similarity, and candidate margins to select or reject. The existing local Q8 LLM must return exactly one of five labels, then the program wraps the shared contract. All methods share rejection rules, so results describe method-plus-rule behavior. Initial JSON requests failed all three LLM positives; one format repair produced three valid labels but only two correct. It failed the enablement gate and remains research-only/default-off.

Delivery check: never credit all shared-guard successes to the model.
Sources:
  https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2/tree/1110a243fdf4706b3f48f1d95db1a4f5529b4d41
  config/embedding.json
  config/llm_local_provenance.json
  config/llm_local_feasibility_v1.json

────────────────────────────────

Slide 8 — Evaluation protocol and overall results (75 s)

The final test has 60 cases: 30 supported and 30 outside scope, plus 18 separate development examples. Test hashes froze before running and all returns were retained. Agent-drafted labels lack human review, so results are exploratory. Overall behavior combines supported correct IDs and unsupported correct rejections: exact 38, MiniLM 47, LLM 48. Error is wrong, not successful rejection. Equal denominators still hide error types. This tests English-to-ID, not comprehensibility.

Delivery check: how would rejecting everything score on supported inputs?
Sources:
  results/evaluation/test-20261008T142047221403Z/summary.json
  results/evaluation/test-20261008T142047221403Z/raw.jsonl
  data/source_manifest.json
  docs/source-review.en.md

────────────────────────────────

Slide 9 — Negative results and default selection (75 s)

LLM's higher total includes one wrong supported ID, two invalid outputs, and two unsupported executions. MiniLM still rejects 13 supported cases, so it is not already excellent. Only 35 LLM cases actually call the model; guards end 25. Correct behavior is 25/35 for received HTTP and 23/25 for guards. These are selected conditional subsets, not independent model-population accuracy. Failures remain, final-set prompts were not tuned, and exact/MiniLM stay the default choices.

Delivery check: why is higher total accuracy insufficient for enablement?

  results/evaluation/test-20261008T142047221403Z/summary.json

Slide 10 — Live demo sequence (80 s)

Start run_demo.command and check localhost port 5412. Enter Thank you: selection succeeds but default preview blocks. Enable research preview for the actual MuJoCo prerender. Use Many thanks with MiniLM for the same meaning. Enter I do not want to wait or Please wait and take two pills; check rejection and clearing prior motion. Offline, installed models/MP4 support exact/MiniLM backup; LLM is unavailable by default. Video playback is not live physical control.

Delivery check: does a failing input leave old motion visible?

Slide 11 — Historical six-person handoff (60 s)

Divide by data/interfaces, not code volume. A1 verifies meaning/source, A2 constrained trajectories. B1/B2 use development data and freeze versions for C1; C2 integrates UI, reproduction, demo. An agent-generated file does not mean a teammate understands it: everyone explains inputs/outputs/failures. Historical plan: complete demo/backup by late October, freeze by November 2. Briefing deadline is November 3; check latest Canvas submission instructions. Current assignments are superseded by the ten-intent guide.

Delivery check: name the next acceptable file/behavior, not just “working on it.”

Slide 12 — Closing and Q&A (40 s)

We completed runnable limited-ID selection and genuine robot kinematic previews, recording differences between three text methods under one protocol. Failures are traceable, but language comprehensibility remains unconfirmed. Next prioritize human labels, second-machine reproduction, and uncaptioned ASL-user paraphrases. If users cannot be recruited, retain the conclusion of video-referenced candidate motions. Keep text accuracy, geometry, actual control, and language comprehension separate in Q&A.

Delivery check: software “passed” cannot answer language/clinical questions.
